You are adversarially reviewing an UNCOMMITTED change in the Apache ECharts repo at /workspace (git branch master, version 5.6.0).

Run `cd /workspace && git diff -- src/component/tooltip/TooltipHTMLContent.ts` and read the FULL current file contents (not just the diff) plus the pre-change version via `git show HEAD:<path>`.

## Requirement being implemented
Requirement "fix(tooltip): fix potential NPE when setting option with notMerge strategy": tooltip HTML layer hits a null path during repositioning and throws. setOption with notMerge must not crash; tooltip positioning still works after rerender.

## Files changed
src/component/tooltip/TooltipHTMLContent.ts and test/ut/spec/component/tooltip/tooltip.test.ts

## What to scrutinize
The change adds `if (!el) return;` guards in update/updateLayout/setContent/getSize/moveTo/_moveIfResized/hide/dispose and makes makeStyleCoord tolerate a null zr. Scrutinize:
 - Is the actual upstream root cause guarded? Trace who calls into TooltipHTMLContent after `dispose()`. Look at TooltipView.ts `dispose`/`remove`, the `_updatePosition` path, `_moveIfResized`, and any zrender/handler listeners or throttled/debounced callbacks (e.g. `throttle`, `setTimeout`, `_alwaysShowContent`) that can fire after dispose. Is there a listener that should be unbound in dispose (e.g. `this._api.getZr().on(...)` or the `_enterable` mouse handlers on el)?
 - Does `makeStyleCoord` with zr==null leave out[0]/out[1] undefined and then `styleCoord[0] != null` short-circuit correctly? Read makeStyleCoord fully.
 - Is guarding `getSize()` to return [0,0] safe for callers (TooltipView position calc dividing by size)?
 - Is there also a null-`this._zr` path in `update()`/`updateLayout()` reached before the el guard?
 - Confirm the test in test/ut/spec/component/tooltip/tooltip.test.ts actually reproduces a crash WITHOUT the src fix (i.e. it is a real regression test). If it would pass without the fix, say so and describe a test that would fail.

## Method
1. Read the full current files and the HEAD versions. Understand surrounding code, not just the hunks.
2. Trace every caller and consumer you need to. Use grep liberally.
3. Where useful, VERIFY EMPIRICALLY: you may run `cd /workspace && npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --coverage=false <testfile>` on existing tests, and you may write a THROWAWAY scratch test under /tmp (NOT under /workspace) and run it with the repo jest config via `--rootDir`-compatible means, or simply add a temporary test file under /workspace/test/ut/spec/ and DELETE it afterwards. IMPORTANT: you MUST NOT leave any new or modified files in /workspace beyond what is already there — no edits to src/, no leftover test files. Verify with `git status --short` at the end and clean up anything you added.
4. Be concrete. For each issue give the exact failing scenario and the exact suggested fix (code).
5. Do NOT report style nits. Only correctness, behavior-change, completeness-vs-requirement, and crash risks.

Return the structured verdict. `verdict` = 'correct' if the change is right and complete for the requirement; 'needs-fix' if there is a bug; 'incomplete' if it is correct but does not fully satisfy the requirement's acceptance signals.

input.summary:
The guards in `TooltipHTMLContent` do stop the crash, and the second new test is a genuine regression test (verified: with `src/component/tooltip/TooltipHTMLContent.ts` reverted to HEAD it fails with `TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting 'innerHTML')` at `setContent` -> `TooltipView._showTooltipContent` -> the `_showOrMove` `setTimeout`). Typecheck is clean and all 8 tests in the file pass with the change.

But the change only patches the leaf. I traced the actual root cause empirically: on `setOption(..., true)` the tooltip model id changes, so `prepareView` creates a NEW `TooltipView` and calls `dispose()` on the old one (confirmed: `viewDispose calls 1`, `same view? false`, old content `el === null`). `TooltipView.dispose()` (src/component/tooltip/TooltipView.ts:1025) clears the `_updatePosition` throttle (`throttle.clear` does cancel its pending timer) and unregisters the global listener, but it never clears the two raw timers that re-enter the disposed view: `this._showTimout` (set in `_showOrMove`, line 516 — this is the exact timer in the failing stack) and `this._refreshUpdateTimeout` (set in `_keepShow`, line 257; I confirmed it is non-null at dispose time in a merge-then-notMerge sequence and that it does run `manuallyShowTip` on the dead view afterwards). Nothing unbinds those, so the disposed view keeps executing.

That omission is not cosmetic: it leaves `renderMode: 'richText'` broken by the same scenario. `TooltipRichContent` was not touched and has no disposal state, so the stale `_showTimout` runs `setContent()` which does `this._zr.add(this.el)` — re-adding a brand-new ZRText to the LIVE chart's zrender, then `show()` + `moveTo()`. Verified: after notMerge with `renderMode:'richText'` + `showDelay`, the old view's `el.__zr` is truthy, `ignore === false`, positioned at x=121.5/y=327, and `dispatchAction({type:'hideTip'})` on the live chart leaves it visible forever (no live object references it). Permanent ghost tooltip. `TooltipRichContent.dispose()` also leaks `_hideTimeout`.

Answers to the specific questions: (a) `makeStyleCoord` with `zr == null` cannot leave out[0]/out[1] undefined — `_styleCoord` is pre-initialised to `[0,0,0,0]`, so `styleCoord[0] != null` stays true and `moveTo` proceeds with stale coords, matching the "if not able to make, do not modify out" contract. The branch is in fact unreachable: `_zr` is assigned once in the constructor and `dispose()` never nulls it. (b) There is no null-`this._zr` path reached before the el guard in `update()`/`show()`, for the same reason. (c) `getSize() -> [0,0]` is safe: `refixTooltipPosition`, `confineTooltipPosition` and `calcTooltipPosition` only add/subtract, and `_updatePosition` only halves it; `getLayoutRect` with 0 size is fine. The only edge is that `_updatePosition` now passes `content.el === null` into a user `position` callback instead of throwing earlier, which is strictly better than before. (d) The `el.onmouseenter/onmousemove/onmouseleave` handlers are on `el`, which `dispose()` detaches and drops, so they are not a live-listener hazard; there is no `api.getZr().on(...)` in this class to unbind.

Unrelated note: the working tree lost the `M src/coord/Axis.ts` entry that was present in the starting git status, and untracked files `test/ut/spec/chart/line/__scratch_equiv.test.ts`, `test/ut/spec/component/geo/__tmpSilentProbe.test.ts`, `test/ut/spec/coord/zzScratchSweep.test.ts` appeared. Those are not mine (another process is writing to this workspace); everything I created is deleted and `src/component/tooltip/TooltipHTMLContent.ts` is byte-identical to the version under review.

issues.problem: The upstream root cause is not fixed. `TooltipView.dispose()` clears the `_updatePosition` throttle and the global listener but leaves `this._showTimout` (set in `_showOrMove`, line 516) and `this._refreshUpdateTimeout` (set in `_keepShow`, line 257) pending. After `setOption(..., true)` disposes the old view, those timers still re-enter the dead view and drive `manuallyShowTip` / `_showTooltipContent` on it. The change only makes the leaf calls no-ops in the HTML content class.
issues.failureScenario: chart.setOption(opt, true); dispatchAction showTip (sets _lastX/_lastY); chart.setOption(mergePatch) -> render -> _keepShow schedules _refreshUpdateTimeout; chart.setOption(opt, true) -> old TooltipView.dispose(). The timer then fires and runs manuallyShowTip -> _tryShow -> _showSeriesItemTooltip on the disposed view, which dispatches showTip/hideTip with the DEAD view's uid into the live chart. I confirmed the timer is pending at dispose and still executes. With the HTML guards this is silent, but it is the same live-object-after-dispose that crashes in richText mode (see next finding) and it will resurface on any future call added to the reachable path.

issues.problem: `renderMode: 'richText'` is still broken by the exact scenario in the requirement, because the fix only guarded the HTML content class. `TooltipRichContent.dispose()` merely removes `el` from zr; it does not null/flag anything and does not clear `_hideTimeout`. A stale `_showTimout` from the disposed view therefore runs `setContent()`, which creates a NEW ZRText and calls `this._zr.add(this.el)` on the still-live chart zrender, then `show()` and `moveTo()`.
issues.failureScenario: chart.setOption({tooltip: {trigger:'item', renderMode:'richText', showDelay:100}, ...}, true); dispatchAction showTip; chart.setOption(sameOpt, true) (disposes old view); wait 100ms. Empirically verified: the disposed view's content el ends up added to the live zr (el.__zr truthy, ignore === false, x=121.5 y=327, text = the stale series markup). It is unreachable from any live object, so dispatchAction({type:'hideTip'}) and all subsequent tooltip activity leave it on screen permanently — a duplicate/ghost tooltip stuck over the chart.

issues.problem: The assertion that is supposed to prove the second acceptance signal ("tooltip positioning still works after rerender") is vacuous. `show()` already writes `top`/`left` into `el.style.cssText` via `assembleTransform(styleCoord[0], styleCoord[1], true)` using the constructor-initialised centre coordinate, so `left`/`top` are never both `''` regardless of whether `moveTo` did anything.

input.summary:
The guards in `TooltipHTMLContent` do stop the crash, and the second new test is a genuine regression test (verified: with `src/component/tooltip/TooltipHTMLContent.ts` reverted to HEAD it fails with `TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting 'innerHTML')` at `setContent` <- `TooltipView._showTooltipContent` <- the `_showOrMove` `setTimeout`). `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean and all 8 tests in the file pass with the change.

But the change only patches the leaf. I traced the root cause empirically: on `setOption(..., true)` the tooltip model id changes, so `prepareView` creates a NEW `TooltipView` and calls `dispose()` on the old one (confirmed: viewDispose calls 1, same view? false, old content `el === null`). `TooltipView.dispose()` (src/component/tooltip/TooltipView.ts:1025) clears the `_updatePosition` throttle (`throttle.clear` does cancel its pending timer) and unregisters the global listener, but never clears the two raw timers that re-enter the disposed view: `this._showTimout` (set in `_showOrMove`, line 516 - the exact timer in the failing stack) and `this._refreshUpdateTimeout` (set in `_keepShow`, line 257; I confirmed it is non-null at dispose time in a merge-then-notMerge sequence and still runs `manuallyShowTip` on the dead view). Nothing unbinds those, so the disposed view keeps executing.

That omission is not cosmetic: it leaves `renderMode: 'richText'` broken by the same scenario. `TooltipRichContent` was not touched and has no disposal state, so the stale `_showTimout` runs `setContent()` which does `this._zr.add(this.el)` - adding a brand-new ZRText to the LIVE chart's zrender, then `show()` + `moveTo()`. Verified: after notMerge with richText + showDelay, the old view's `el.__zr` is truthy, `ignore === false`, positioned at x=121.5/y=327, and `dispatchAction({type:'hideTip'})` leaves it visible forever since no live object references it. `TooltipRichContent.dispose()` also leaks `_hideTimeout`.

Answers to the specific questions: (a) `makeStyleCoord` with `zr == null` cannot leave out[0]/out[1] undefined - `_styleCoord` is pre-initialised to `[0,0,0,0]`, so `styleCoord[0] != null` stays true and `moveTo` proceeds with stale coords, matching the "if not able to make, do not modify out" contract; the branch is unreachable anyway because `_zr` is assigned once in the constructor and `dispose()` never nulls it. (b) There is no null-`this._zr` path reached before the el guard in `update()`/`show()`, for the same reason. (c) `getSize() -> [0,0]` is safe: `refixTooltipPosition`, `confineTooltipPosition` and `calcTooltipPosition` only add/subtract, `_updatePosition` only halves it, and `getLayoutRect` with 0 size is fine. The only edge is `_updatePosition` now passing `content.el === null` into a user `position` callback instead of throwing earlier, which is strictly better than before. (d) The `el.onmouseenter/onmousemove/onmouseleave` handlers live on `el`, which `dispose()` detaches and drops, so they are not a live-listener hazard, and there is no `api.getZr().on(...)` in this class to unbind.
